title: Practice-based evidence complements not replaces evidence-based practice
‘Nothing About him and Everything About you’: A Framework of Recovery Strategies from IPV in the Context of Online Discussion Forums
abstract: Abstract Purpose While research has examined women’s help-seeking and recovery from intimate partner violence (IPV), less attention has been given to these processes in online discussions, particularly for Jewish-identified women. This study examined how Jewish women in Montreal described their experiences of help-seeking for IPV during the initial waves of COVID-19, with specific attention to recovery through online discussion forums. Methods The sample included 79 adult women from three Jewish congregations in Montreal, Canada, participating in remote focus groups and face-to-face interviews conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. Data were analyzed using Reflective Thematic Analysis. Trustworthiness was established in accordance with Shenton’s criteria, through peer debriefing, and reflexivity. Results Three interrelated themes emerged characterizing women’s recovery journeys during social distancing and lockdowns: (1) ‘What should you do’ (doing); (2) ‘What you should not do’ (avoidance); and (3) ‘What should you accept’ (acceptance). Findings revealed a deep focus of online support, incorporating both universal and religious aspects of recovery. Conclusions The findings demonstrate that during periods of enforced social isolation, online discussion forums play a decisive role in shaping IPV recovery strategies. For women from religious minority communities, self-focused recovery strategies offered an accessible pathway to self-directed healing. The study underscores the need for culturally responsive approaches to online support for Jewish women experiencing IPV, with broader relevance for contexts of social crisis in which formal services are severely restricted.

title: Where health-care AI ethics becomes public: documentation as ethics infrastructure in open-source repositories
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how ethical concerns about open-source artificial intelligence (AI) artefacts become publicly sustained and incorporated into documentation, with implications for health-care organisations procuring and governing components they did not build. Design/methodology/approach Comparative case study of four GitHub repositories (January 2020 to January 2025): Fairlearn, AI Fairness 360 (AIF360), Clinical Bidirectional encoder representations from transformers (BERT) and BioBERT. The corpus comprises 450 keyword-retained issue threads and 2,136 within-window comments, analysed through Big Q reflexive thematic analysis, a transparent marker audit and cross-case pattern matching. Findings Fairlearn repeatedly converts data set, terminology, intended-use and metric-interpretation debates into documentation. AIF360 raises comparable data set-provenance and metric-interpretation concerns, but they receive brief or no replies and are rarely carried into linked guidance. The clinical repositories are not silent: model-validity and intended-use concerns appear, including sustained BioBERT discussion, but they are weakly classified and unevenly carried into durable guidance. The pattern is associated with maintenance capacity, contributor pathways, issue classification and cross-channel coordination; the design does not isolate resourcing from topic or repository genre. Practical implications Health-care AI procurement should distinguish an artefact’s ethical labels from the upstream processes that produced them. Provisional audit prompts indicate where ethical reasoning is publicly inspectable; they are not a validated procurement instrument. Originality/value Documentation as ethics infrastructure names the practices through which ethical reasoning becomes durable and publicly inspectable. The translation gap is advanced as a downstream proposition requiring procurement-side testing, rather than as an outcome directly observed in these repositories.

title: Theoretical, practical and normative dimensions of value concepts and valuation methods in B2B marketing
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to show that value concepts can provide marketing action with meaning, and that this meaning is related to the self-conception of marketing as being valuable for individual and organizational actors, as well as society, the former addressed in terms of private value and the latter in terms of nonprivate value. The paper also demonstrates how value concepts align with theories generated in marketing and beyond. Design/methodology/approach This paper investigates the role of value concepts in guiding marketing actions and the interplay between value concepts and valuation in B2B marketing. Using methodological insights into conceptual work in marketing, it discusses empirical and philosophical theories to analyze the interpretation and use of value concepts and related valuation models in B2B marketing. Two new conceptual distinctions are introduced. The analysis yields eight theoretical propositions that synthesize the insights gained. Findings In the context of socioeconomic action, value concepts are specific interpretations of the reasons for, intentions behind or desired outcomes of actions. Rather than being summations of valuation processes, value concepts structure and guide them. Complex, interrelated valuation processes and the operations considered by them are undertheorized in B2B marketing. Valuation models do not represent essential relational dimensions of transactions and relationships. Societal value is not fully reflected in the value concepts widely used in the B2B community. Research limitations/implications B2B marketing research must develop adequate valuation models that account for the relational dimensions of transactions, relationships and other socioeconomic entities. Furthermore, two underresearched areas require further exploration. The first is the integration of social or nonprivate value into value concepts, valuation models and valuations. The second is the specification of a fuller variety of axiological values beyond efficiency and effectiveness, related to the previously mentioned objective of bringing about social or nonprivate values. Practical implications It is the B2B marketing community, which includes scholars and practitioners, that crafts value concepts and realizes their potential. The community can synthesize knowledge to address the relational nature of its theoretical conceptualizations and practical research units. Different categories of values can be incorporated into its analyses, communications and policies. Value concepts can also be leveraged to guide managerial decision-making. Originality/value This paper examines value and valuation in B2B marketing from theoretical, methodological and normative perspectives. It bridges the relational perspectives in marketing, economics and sociology. It argues that the ethical or ecological “goodness” of relational perspectives is not inherent in relationality itself but rather emerges from reference to axiological values in valuation processes.

title: The Xylanase Effector Xyn1 from Ceratocystis fimbriata Promotes Virulence by Triggering Host Ferroptosis through the SSL3 Domain
journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
abstract: Abstract Sweetpotato black rot, caused by the necrotrophic fungus Ceratocystis fimbriata, is a devastating global disease with unclear pathogenesis. In this study, we identified 108 candidate effectors from genomic/transcriptomic data, characterizing xylanase Xyn1 as a key virulence factor inducing ferroptosis-like cell death in Nicotiana benthamiana and sweetpotato. Its SSL3 domain, conserved only in a few Ceratocystis species, is necessary and sufficient for cell death-inducing activity and full virulence. Xyn1 triggers ferroptosis, marked by membrane damage, lipid peroxidation, and reduced glutathione (GSH) depletion; ferroptosis inhibitors Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) and Deferoxamine (DFO) suppressed ferroptosis and pathogenicity. Xyn1 interacts with host farnesyltransferase subunit NbFTA1 via its SSL3 domain, whose silencing alleviated ferroptosis. Collectively, these findings preliminarily elucidate a novel biochemical mechanism by which a fungal xylanase effector directly targets the host farnesyltransferase subunit to induce ferroptosis, providing an effective antiferroptosis-based strategy against sweetpotato black rot and potential molecular targets for breeding disease-resistant sweetpotato varieties.

title: The Digital Infrastructure Construction and Regional Income Gap
journal: Advances in Economics, Management and Political Sciences
abstract: As the material carrier of the growth of the digital economy, how digital infrastructure development affects regional income gap has become a frontier topic in the cross field of development economics and regional economics. Digital infrastructure was only a kind of communication network at the earliest, and now it has developed into a new infrastructure system with 5G, Gigabit optical network, computing power network, data infrastructure with so on. Digital infrastructure has expanded information availability, reduced transaction costs, promoted industrial upgrading, and improved public services. Yet it can also create a digital divide arising from differences in regional construction capabilities, digital skills, and industrial agglomeration. In recent years, as the advancement of China's Broadband China and other strategies, the research scale has further sunk from the transnational and provincial levels to the prefecture and city level, and the marginal effect, spatial spillover and digital transmission infrastructure have become new research hotspots. The association of digital infrastructure and regional income inequality may vary in developmental stages. Only when network coverage can be transformed into application ability, employment opportunities and industrial undertaking ability, will it have the effect of inclusive growth.
